verdicts.title: DP-SGD resume keeps the checkpoint's Poisson sample_rate in the sampler but rebuilds the accountant from the new args, so a batch-size change on resume under-reports epsilon behind a log.warning
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree with the finding's own script (rate3.py) under `uv run`. Every link of the chain verified independently in the current source: (1) `_from_state_dict_poisson` (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:229-266) rebuilds the sampler with `sample_rate=float(sd["sample_rate"])` and `truncated_batch_size=sd.get("truncated_batch_size")` from the SNAPSHOT, taking only `n_steps` and the dataset from the template, and its only equality guard is `num_samples`. (2) `_build_mechanism` (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4525-4545) closes the accountant's `dpsgd_acc.poisson(...)` over the CURRENT `sample_rate` (`ctx.sample_rate = train_batch_size / effective_dataset_size`). (3) `RuntimeCheckpoint.sample_rate` is tagged `drift="dp_relevant"` (_checkpoint.py:232-234) and `_warn_on_arg_drift` (_dp_trainer.py:5679-5760) raises only when `saved_mechanism != "gaussian" or horizon_resume`; for plain Poisson DP-SGD it emits `log.warning` and continues. (4) `truncated_batch_size` is indeed absent from `RuntimeCheckpoint`'s field list, so drifting it warns nothing at all. (5) The #1019 guard exists only in `_k_out_of_t.py:204-212` (`for name in ("k","t","allocation") ... raise ConfigurationError`). Note the sampler-side behaviour is deliberate and pinned by packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/sampling/test_poisson_state_dict.py:88-106 (`test_round_trip_preserves_truncated_batch_size` asserts `restored.sample_rate == 0.2` against a template built at 0.5), so the defect is the trainer-level desync between two individually-intentional choices, not the codec alone; the finding's fix sketch would have to change that test. No open tracked issue covers it (milestones-open.tsv / other-open-issues.tsv checked; #792 and #1019 are closed). Kept at high rather than critical because a diagnostic IS printed and the direction is fail-open only when the resume batch size is SMALLER; a larger resume batch size over-charges epsilon (conservative).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Reproduced verbatim on HEAD (gpt2+LoRA, N=64, privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0, sampling_mode=poisson default, save_steps=4, use_cpu). Phase 1 at per_device_train_batch_size=32 (q=0.5) realises batch sizes [32,25,29,31,36,26,41,36] and reports privacy_epsilon=4.75151. Resuming checkpoint-4 with per_device_train_batch_size=8 (q=0.125) realises [36,26,41,36] for steps 5-8 - bit-identical to the continuous q=0.5 run, proving the restored sampler is still drawing Bernoulli(0.5) - yet reports privacy_epsilon=3.25344, i.e. 31.5% below the epsilon of the mechanism that actually ran. The post-resume steps each add ~0.025 to epsilon instead of ~0.40. The only diagnostics are three log.warning lines ('Resume arg drift on sample_rate (dp_relevant, DP-SGD): saved=0.5, current=0.125', plus expected_steps_per_epoch and expected_batch_size); none states which value won or that the reported epsilon no longer bounds the executed mechanism. Reaching it requires a user to change per_device_train_batch_size (or the dataset-size denominator) on resume of a Poisson DP-SGD run - a common operational action, all-default sampling mode. The reverse change (larger resume batch) is conservative, not fail-open. `truncated_batch_size` drift is the same desync with zero diagnostics, since it is not a RuntimeCheckpoint field.

verdicts.title: Full-finetune resume and load_best_model_at_end crash for every tied-embedding model because the checkpoint omits lm_head.weight but the loader is strict
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced twice on the current tree. (a) Trainer level, gpt2 full finetune (no PEFT), 4 steps / save_steps=2: `trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=.../checkpoint-2)` raises `RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict for GPT2LMHeadModel: Missing key(s) in state_dict: "lm_head.weight"` from packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5481. (b) Trainer level for a SUPPORTED family: I wrote a fresh script using `LlamaConfig(tie_word_embeddings=True)` full finetune; phase 1 saves checkpoint-2 with ['accountant.json','config.json','dp_optimizer.pt','dp_state.pt','model.safetensors',...] and resume fails with `Missing key(s) in state_dict: "lm_head.weight"` for LlamaForCausalLM. (c) Mechanism confirmed in isolation on transformers 5.15.1: `_tied_weights_keys == {'lm_head.weight': 'model.embed_tokens.weight'}`, `save_pretrained` writes 11 tensors with `lm_head.weight` absent while `model.state_dict()` contains it, so `load_state_dict(..., strict=True)` raises. Code path verified: `_save_model_artifacts` (_dp_trainer.py:5242-5247) uses `self._model.save_pretrained(...)`; `_load_model_weights` (:5469-5481) and `_load_best_model` (:4892-4912) both set `strict = not self._is_peft` and pass the loaded dict straight to `load_state_dict`; neither calls `tie_weights()` nor filters `_tied_weights_keys`. The sharded branch of `_read_weights_file` uses `strict=False`, so only the single-file (i.e. normal small/medium model) path is affected. Why no test catches it: every resume test in packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_dp_trainer.py uses the `gpt2_with_lora` fixture, i.e. PEFT, where `strict=False`. One correction to the finding: `tie_word_embeddings` is NOT the class default for LlamaConfig/Qwen2Config/Qwen3Config (all False on 5.15.1) - it is the default for GPT2Config and Gemma2Config and is set True in the published config.json of many real Hub checkpoints (Gemma/Gemma2/Gemma3, SmolLM, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B). Not epsilon-affecting and loud rather than silent, but it breaks a documented core workflow. No open tracked issue matches.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any non-PEFT (full-finetune) DPTrainer run whose model has tied input/output embeddings - verified for GPT2LMHeadModel and for `LlamaConfig(tie_word_embeddings=True)`, and true for every Gemma/Gemma2/Gemma3 config and for the published tied checkpoints of Llama-3.2 / Qwen3 / SmolLM. `_save_model_artifacts` calls `save_pretrained`, which drops the tied key from model.safetensors; `_load_model_weights` then calls `load_state_dict(new_state, strict=True)` because `self._is_peft` is False, and resume dies with `RuntimeError: ... Missing key(s) in state_dict: "lm_head.weight"` at _dp_trainer.py:5481 before the first post-resume step. The identical code in `_load_best_model` (:4910-4912) means a full-finetune run with `load_best_model_at_end=True` crashes at the END of training, after the privacy budget has already been spent and after the weights were saved, so the run's result is unrecoverable through the trainer. Only single-file checkpoints are affected; the sharded path already loads with strict=False. Not a privacy defect.

verdicts.title: MF noise state carries no derivation-version or execution-identity tag except for BISR, so the #1018 lambda-CGD stream change and any strategy-hyperparameter drift restore silently onto a different mechanism
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanical claims are all true and I reproduced the finding's accept/reject matrix exactly by re-running its t3.py on HEAD: band_mf n_steps 8->16 ACCEPTED with different noise (-0.76381 -> -0.70943), band_mf momentum 1.0->0.5 ACCEPTED (-0.76381 -> -1.01377), bsr alpha 0.9->0.7 ACCEPTED (-1.10275 -> -1.03146), lambda_cgd lambda_ 0.5->0.9 ACCEPTED (-1.27672 -> -1.77366), while bands/bandwidth drift is caught incidentally by inner-state shape checks and only BISR rejects via `_BisrExecutionIdentity`. The version facts also hold: `git log -S"_LAYOUT_VERSION" -- _state_codec.py` returns only 1794504b (#901), f2d90d61 (#1018) changed lambda-CGD from `rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)` to `_mf_gaussian_column_key(st._rng_key, step)` in _lambda_cgd.py without touching `_LAYOUT_VERSION` (still 1); DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION is 7 at v0.15.4/v0.15.5.rc1/v0.15.5.rc2/v0.15.6.rc1 and 8 at HEAD. HOWEVER the finding's severity and its characterisation of the trainer as protected 'only by coincidence' are wrong, and I refuted that half by running two real trainer resumes: (a) mf_band with privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs momentum 1.0 -> 0.5 and (b) mf_lambda_cgd with lambda_ 0.5 -> 0.9. BOTH are rejected with `CheckpointError: Whole-horizon resume forbids drift on 'horizon_process_state': saved={'type': 'CyclicPoisson', 'inner': {'type': 'MfGaussian', ..., 'strategy': {'type': 'BandMfStrategy', 'bands': 2, 'momentum': 1.0, ...}}}` / `{'type': 'LambdaCgdStrategy', 'lambda_': 0.5, 'normalized': True, ...}`. `horizon_process_state` is a `compare_on_resume` / `dp_relevant` field (_checkpoint.py:271-274) carrying the FULL serialised strategy, and `_initialize_accounting` (_dp_trainer.py:275-281) returns a non-None horizon_process for every mf_* mechanism, so `_warn_on_arg_drift` raises rather than warns for any non-gaussian mechanism_kind. The trainer therefore fails closed on the entire class of strategy-hyperparameter drift, plus mf_n_steps/mf_min_sep/mf_max_participations and the bundle version. What remains is (i) the direct-library path, which MFNoiseState's own docstring (_engine.py:57-63) explicitly assigns to the caller ('standalone callers are responsible for preserving the same construction inputs'), and (ii) the genuinely un-delegatable case: a library-direct caller who DOES preserve every construction input but upgrades opaque across #1018 gets a silently different lambda-CGD stream, which `_LAYOUT_VERSION` exists to catch. #1018 is in no release tag (`git tag --contains f2d90d61` is empty; `git describe` = v0.15.6.rc1-2-gf2d90d61), so no released version pair can hit it today. Low, not medium. No open tracked issue matches (#319 is the DP-FTRL mechanism/strategy-invariants umbrella but is about mechanism math, not state versioning).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Reachable only through direct library use of `opaque.dpftrl.noise` + `opaque.serialization`, not through DPTrainer. Verified accepted-without-error on HEAD: an MFNoiseState saved at step 3 and restored into a template built with a different `n_steps` (band_mf 8->16), `momentum` (1.0->0.5), `alpha` (bsr 0.9->0.7) or `lambda_` (0.5->0.9) is accepted verbatim and the next release differs from the uninterrupted run, so the realised linear operator is a hybrid of two strategies while an accountant built for the new strategy prices the whole horizon. Separately, `_LAYOUT_VERSION` was not bumped when #1018 changed lambda-CGD's per-step key derivation, so a state written by a pre-#1018 build and restored by HEAD is accepted and emits a different stream even though the caller preserved every construction input; because C^-1 is 2-banded for lambda-CGD the resume-step correlation term multiplies a z_{s-1} that was never released. Both are confined to the standalone path: MFNoiseState's docstring declares construction-input preservation the standalone caller's responsibility, and DPTrainer resume rejects every one of these drifts with CheckpointError on `horizon_process_state` (verified for mf_band momentum and mf_lambda_cgd lambda_) as well as on the dp_state bundle version (7 at every release tag in the delta vs 8 at HEAD). #1018 is in no released tag, so the cross-version stream break has no released victim today.

verdicts.title: DDP resume installs rank 0's sampler snapshot on every rank, silently re-correlating the per-rank Poisson masks that the per-rank key fold exists to keep independent
verdicts.reasoning: The finding said the two-rank reproduction was not run and the magnitude was reasoned; I ran both. (1) Real 2-rank Gloo DDP run (packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py fixtures, world_size=2, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2, use_cpu): fresh phase stream keys are per-rank distinct (rank0 seed 1950457451192556855, rank1 seed 16528425509808239245); after resume BOTH ranks report seed 1950457451192556855. Rank 0's key is installed on every rank, exactly as the in-code caveat says. (2) Code path verified: the per-rank fold is `sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)` guarded by `if self._ddp.world_size > 1` (_dp_trainer.py:3944-3949); the snapshot is written only under `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` (:5151, calling `_save_dp_runtime` at :5197), and `should_save` returns `ddp.is_world_zero` by default (_distributed.py:211-222); the restore `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` (:1874-1876) is guarded only by `resume_path is not None and saved_sampler_state is not None and not a.ignore_data_skip` - no rank branch. `local_shard` gives contiguous disjoint shards (_shard.py:20-35), so 'same local index' is a fixed group of world_size records. (3) I also refuted the in-code justification at :3872-3874 ('the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected') numerically. Under the shared mask the mechanism Poisson-samples GROUPS of W co-indexed records, so for neighbouring D / D u {x} the conditional pair is (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(a,s) vs (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(a+1,s) with a = (W-1) worst-case aligned clipped gradients (units of C/B, s = noise_multiplier), instead of the amplified pair N(0,s) vs (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(1,s). Numerically integrating both hockey-stick divergences: at noise_multiplier=1.0, q=0.01, world_size=4, eps=1 the executed mechanism's per-step delta is 1.26e-3 while the amplified mechanism the accountant prices gives 2.73e-9 (ratio 4.6e5); at nm=1.0, q=0.1, W=4, eps=1 it is 1.27e-2 vs 2.07e-4; at nm=2.0, q=0.1, W=8, eps=1 it is 6.8e-4 vs 1.1e-10. In the well-separated regime the executed delta converges to exactly q * delta_Gaussian(unamplified) - i.e. subsampling buys only the factor q, not the subsampled-Gaussian bound. Amplification requires the target record's inclusion indicator to be independent of the rest of the sample, which the shared mask destroys; the marginal being Bernoulli(q) is not sufficient. Raised from medium to high: default `ignore_data_skip=False`, default `save_on_each_node=False`, ordinary DDP + resume, no warning, fail-open, and the source comment asserts the opposite. Not in milestones-open.tsv or other-open-issues.tsv (the FSDP2 issues #55-58 are a different subject), so the in-code 'tracked for the multi-GPU work' is not backed by an open issue I can find.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Any DPTrainer DDP run (world_size > 1, default save_on_each_node=False, default ignore_data_skip=False) with per-record Bernoulli sampling (poisson or cyclic_poisson) that is resumed from a checkpoint. Measured on a real 2-rank Gloo run: the fresh phase gives each rank a distinct sampler stream key (fold_in(seed, rank)), but after `resume_from_checkpoint` every rank restores the rank-0 snapshot's key_seed, so all ranks draw the identical Bernoulli(q) mask over their own disjoint contiguous shard and the world_size records sharing a local index are included or excluded together for every post-resume step. The accountant keeps charging the i.i.d.-Poisson-amplified per-step PLD. Quantified by numerically integrating the hockey-stick divergence of the group-sampled mechanism against the amplified one, with worst-case aligned co-indexed gradients: at noise_multiplier=1.0, q=0.01, world_size=4 the real per-step delta at eps=1 is 1.26e-3 versus the charged 2.73e-9; at q=0.1 it is 1.27e-2 versus 2.07e-4. In the separated regime the real cost is q * delta_Gaussian(unamplified), so the reported epsilon understates the executed mechanism by a margin that grows with world_size and with noise_multiplier. No warning is emitted at resume, no distributed-lane test covers the sampler snapshot, and the source comment at _dp_trainer.py:3872-3874 asserts the accounting is unaffected, which the above refutes. The worst-case magnitude needs an adversarial dataset with aligned co-indexed gradients; the qualitative loss of amplification is unconditional.
